title: Sampling changes the gradient you estimate
promptMarkdown: At a fixed parameter, per-example scalar gradients are(−2,0,2,4). (a) Calculate the empirical mean and variance of one uniform draw. (b) Calculate the variance of the average of two independent draws with replacement. (c) Enumerate all six equally likely unordered batches of two without replacement and find the batch-mean variance. (d) If the last example is sampled with probability 1/2 and the other three each1/6, compute the unweighted expected gradient and explain a correction that restores the uniform empirical objective.
hintLadder: Treat the four gradients as a finite population at a fixed parameter.
Use population denominator4 rather than the sample-unbiased estimator denominator3.
For biased sampling compute the expectation before proposing importance weights.
